newsitem.title: DENMARK: Danish shares down, Thursday outlook grim.
newsitem.headline: Danish shares down, Thursday outlook grim.

text.p: Danish share prices closed lower on Monday, although dealers said they fared better than some foreign markets, but Thursday's outlook seemed gloomy.
"The Dow opened with a fall, bond prices are down and the dollar is weaker. It doesn't look good," a dealer said, adding that a Danish fall of 0.5 to 1.0 point on Thursday appeared realistic.

The KFX top-20 index fell 0.88 point -- 0.66 percent -- to 131.46, in overall bourse turnover of 617 million crowns. The KFX December future fell 1.10 point to 131.00 with 210 contracts each worth 100,000 crowns traded.
"We'll start down tomorrow, no doubt, but how bad it is depends on much the Dow falls," the dealer said.

Shipping group J.Lauritzen soared on Wednesday to 620 crowns from Tuesday's 475 crowns after announcing that it had sold 48 percent of its loss-making Danyard shipyard to a Malaysian company and would sell a further 27 percent.

Radiometer was expected to fall on Thursday after Wednesday's first half result showed profits below expectations and 20 percent lower than the same period the year before. --Claus Mathisen, Copenhagen newsroom +45 33969659
